item.title: The Greek Word That Changed Isaiah 7:14
item.description:
In this clip, Steve Eisenhower breaks down one of the most important translation debates in the Bible: Isaiah 7:14 and the meaning of the Hebrew word almah and the Greek word parthenos.
Was the original prophecy really speaking about a virgin birth, or did the meaning of the Greek word change over time? Steve explains the historical and linguistic background, how parthenos was used in earlier Greek literature, and why this verse became so central to Christian interpretation.
One word can completely change how a prophecy is understood.
@Exodus_Project #Isaiah714 #Bible #Judaism #Christianity #Torah #Prophecy #Hebrew

item.title: 🚨WARNING: What’s Coming Next Is Worse Than You Think
item.description:
What if we are not waiting for Gog and Magog anymore?
Rabbi Efraim Palvanov argues that the prophetic sequence described in Ezekiel may already be unfolding before our eyes. Israel has returned. The land has revived. The Jewish people are gathering from exile. And the confrontation surrounding Iran and Persia may place us somewhere in Ezekiel 38 and 39 right now.
If that is true, the question is no longer whether prophecy is beginning.
The question is: what comes next?
In this powerful conversation, we walk through Ezekiel 36, 37, 38 and 39 and examine where we may actually stand in the redemption process.
Why does Persia appear in the prophecy of Gog and Magog? Could the events surrounding Iran be part of that process? What comes after Ezekiel 38 and 39? And why does Rabbi Palvanov say that we are now “very much at the finish line”?
We also explore one of the most extraordinary ideas in the entire conversation: could the resurrection of the dead eventually involve DNA, biotechnology or future forms of cloning?
In this episode:
• Why Rabbi Palvanov believes we are living in the pre-Messianic era • Ezekiel 36, 37, 38 and 39 • Why Gog and Magog may already be unfolding • The prophetic role of Persia and Iran • The return of the Jewish people to the Land of Israel • What happens after Ezekiel 38 and 39 • The Third Temple and the next stages of redemption • Could resurrection involve DNA and biotechnology? • Why Torah is spreading increasingly to the nations • Why the redemption process may be accelerating
If the prophetic timeline is really where Rabbi Palvanov believes it is, then what comes next could change everything.

item.title: AI Could Make Online Antisemitism MUCH Worse
item.description:
In this clip, Nick Matau and I discuss a disturbing question: as social media platforms rely more heavily on AI and algorithms, could those systems end up amplifying antisemitism simply because outrage and hostility generate engagement?
Nick shares his own experience of having a 230,000-follower Instagram account suddenly removed without warning and says he has been banned from TikTok more than 20 times. He also explains why he believes fighting antisemitism is not only about defending Jews or Israel, but about protecting Western society from a pattern history has seen before.
Can an algorithm actually become biased by the society it learns from?

item.title: 🚨They’re Preparing to Rebuild the Third Temple RIGHT NOW...
item.description:
The rebuilding of the Third Temple is no longer just a theoretical discussion.
Rabbi Yehuda Glick reveals the real preparations already taking place connected to the Beit Hamikdash — including Temple vessels that have already been prepared, Kohanim studying the laws of the Temple service, work on the priestly garments, and groups developing blueprints and practical plans for rebuilding.
He also describes the extraordinary transformation taking place on the Temple Mount itself.
Only a decade ago, Jewish prayer on the Temple Mount was heavily restricted. Today, increasing numbers of Jews are ascending, praying, singing and bowing on Judaism’s holiest site.
In this conversation we discuss:
• The preparations already underway for the Third Temple • Temple vessels that have already been prepared • Blueprints and practical plans for rebuilding • Kohanim preparing for the Temple service • The dramatic changes taking place on the Temple Mount • Why Rabbi Glick believes more Jews must return to the mountain • The Temple Mount as a house of prayer for all nations • Jerusalem, redemption and biblical prophecy • What Rabbi Glick believes needs to happen next
For generations, rebuilding the Beit Hamikdash seemed impossibly distant.
Rabbi Glick believes that is changing.
His message is simple:
“It’s in our hands.”

item.title: Jewish Disagreement May Be Our Greatest Strength
item.description:
Nick Matau offers an unexpected outsider’s perspective on one of the oldest problems in Jewish history: disagreement.
Jewish division has caused enormous problems throughout our history. But Nick argues that the same instinct to question, argue and challenge each other may also be one of the Jewish people’s greatest strengths.
When disagreement is done honestly and in good faith, it forces people to think deeper, challenge assumptions and discover ideas they may never have reached on their own.
Are the Jewish people too divided, or have we misunderstood the power of disagreement?
@NickMatau
#NickMatau #Judaism #Israel #Torah #JewishPeople #JewishWisdom

item.title: 🚨White House Correspondent WARNS We Have VERY LITTLE TIME Left...
item.description:
White House correspondent Jake Turx joins Aron Sokol for a powerful conversation about ancient Jewish prophecy, Israel, the future of the West and the extraordinary events unfolding around the world right now.
After October 7, Jake says he began reading the Nevi’im differently — seeing patterns described by the prophets that seemed remarkably connected to events he was witnessing firsthand.
What did the prophets actually foresee? Why does the Book of Ovadiah focus so intensely on Edom? What role do Edom, Ishmael and the nations of the world play in the final redemption?
And why does Jake warn that “the world as we know it is going to be altered forever” and that “we have very little time”?
In this fascinating conversation, Jake Turx explores the ancient struggle between Edom, Ishmael and Israel, the prophetic meaning he sees in current world events, and why he believes our generation is witnessing patterns described thousands of years ago.
We discuss:
• Why October 7 changed the way Jake began reading the prophets • The Book of Ovadiah and its message about Edom • What Jewish tradition means by the “culture of Edom” • The clash between Edom, Ishmael and Israel • Why the nations are being tested by their response to Israel • The United Nations and the gathering of nations against Israel • Antisemitism and its place in the larger prophetic story • America’s unique role in the Western world • Social media, global news and the spread of knowledge across the world • Why this generation may be seeing biblical prophecy with unprecedented clarity • Jake’s warning about the direction of Western civilization • Why prophecy is not a blueprint for forcing world events • What Jews and non-Jews can do during extraordinary times • Why Jake believes the world in its present form cannot remain unchanged forever
Jake emphasizes that prophecy is not simply about predicting the future. It is about recognizing the deeper direction of history and understanding the choices facing individuals and nations.
Near the end of the conversation, he delivers a striking warning: the world as we know it has a finite amount of time left in its present form. Whether that means weeks, years or decades, Jake believes we are living through a period of enormous historical and spiritual change.
May we all be blessed with clarity to understand the times we are living through, the courage to make the right choices, and the merit to witness the complete redemption, peace for Israel and a world filled with the knowledge of Hashem.
Subscribe to @InspiredIsrael for more conversations about Israel, Jewish prophecy, Moshiach, the Third Temple and the unfolding redemption.
#israel #prophecy #endtimes

item.title: 🚨WARNING: THIS Is TRIGGERING the Coming of Mashiach | Tovia Singer
item.description:
Something remarkable is happening in Israel and Rabbi Tovia Singer believes it may be far more significant than most people realize.
Across Israel, Jews are returning to Torah, reconnecting with their Jewish identity and coming together in ways we have not seen in years. But could this growing spiritual awakening actually be part of the prophetic process leading toward the final redemption?
In this powerful conversation, Rabbi Tovia Singer explains why teshuvah and Jewish unity are directly connected to the coming of Mashiach — and why the changes taking place in Israel right now deserve our attention.
The prophets did not describe redemption as an isolated supernatural event. They described a process: the Jewish people returning to their land, returning to Hashem, rebuilding their nation and ultimately moving toward the complete redemption.
We discuss Isaiah 59 and the coming of the Redeemer, the extraordinary return to Torah taking place in Israel, the growing unity of the Jewish people, the role of Israel in Biblical prophecy, the Noahide movement, Christianity's response to the Jewish return, and why the rebuilding of the Beis Hamikdash remains central to the Biblical vision of redemption.
Rabbi Singer makes an extraordinary point: Mashiach doesn't arrive disconnected from what is happening to the Jewish people.
The pieces have been moving into place.
The Jewish people have returned to Israel. Israel has been rebuilt. The land has come back to life. And now something is happening spiritually.
Are we watching another stage of the redemption unfold before our eyes?
Follow the official Living Inspired channel for more conversations about Israel, Biblical prophecy, Moshiach and the extraordinary events unfolding in our generation.

The first day of Rosh Hashanah 2026 falls on Shabbat, and Rabbi Lawrence Hajioff explains why this year carries such a powerful message.
What is the real meaning of Rosh Hashanah? Why does the Torah describe it as a day of sounding the shofar rather than simply a “Day of Judgment”? And what does the shofar reveal about teshuvah, judgment, redemption and the year ahead?
In this conversation, Rabbi Lawrence Hajioff explores the deeper meaning of Rosh Hashanah, the spiritual significance of listening, and the teaching that Rosh Hashanah is a microcosm of the entire coming year.
We discuss:
• Why the shofar is the central Torah mitzvah of Rosh Hashanah • Why the shofar represents the inner cry of the Jewish soul • The shofar of Mount Sinai and the future shofar of redemption • The Rambam’s famous description of the shofar as a spiritual wake-up call • Why one mitzvah can change a person and impact the entire world • The remarkable lesson of Ishmael and “ba’asher hu sham” • Why a person is judged according to who they are right now • How teshuvah, tefillah and tzedakah can change a difficult decree • The special significance of the first day of Rosh Hashanah 2026 falling on Shabbat • A blessing for a sweet new year, redemption and the rebuilding of the Third Temple
Rosh Hashanah is not simply about fear. It is about renewal. It is the moment when we stop, listen, examine who we are and recognize that the coming year can still be changed.
May we all be written and sealed for a Shana Tova U’Metuka, a good and sweet year filled with blessing, peace and redemption.

item.title: 🚨WARNING: The Third Temple is NEXT...
item.description:
Rabbi Tovia Singer joins Aron Sokol to discuss one of the most controversial questions surrounding the unfolding redemption: what does the Tanakh actually say about the rebuilding of the Third Temple?
Rabbi Singer explains why the Third Temple is not a Jewish plan to dominate the world, but a central part of the biblical vision in which the nations ultimately recognize the God of Israel. He explores Ezekiel 37, Isaiah 56 and Isaiah 60, and explains why the rebuilding of the Temple in Jerusalem would change the religious world forever.
The conversation also explores why Rabbi Singer believes Jerusalem’s return to Jewish control in 1967 helped ignite a worldwide spiritual awakening, the extraordinary growth of the Noahide movement, and why so many former Christians are now turning toward the faith of Israel.
We also discuss the role of the nations in the future redemption, whether non Jews will participate in rebuilding the Third Temple, the significance of Britain and the return of Jewish sovereignty, and why Rabbi Singer believes the prophecies that have not yet been fulfilled will ultimately unfold just as literally as those that already have.
Is the Temple Mount really about takeover, or is the world about to discover something much bigger?

item.title: 🚨The REAL Reason Jews Still Reject Jesus
item.description:
Why have Jews rejected Jesus as the Messiah for almost two thousand years?
The answer is not that Jews have never heard about Jesus, refuse to read the Bible, or hate Christians. The real answer is that Judaism and Christianity disagree about what the Messiah is, what he must accomplish, whether a human being can be divine, and whether the Torah can ever be replaced.
In this episode, Rabbi Aron Sokol presents the Jewish position directly from the Hebrew Bible and the writings of Maimonides. The discussion follows the central framework developed by Rabbi Aryeh Kaplan in his classic work, The Real Messiah.
The prophets gave the Messiah a clear mission. He must gather the Jewish exiles, restore the kingdom of David, rebuild the Temple in Jerusalem, strengthen Torah observance, bring humanity to the knowledge of God, and establish real peace throughout the world.
The central question is simple: Did Jesus complete that mission?
This video examines:
• The traditional Jewish definition of Mashiach • Why Judaism teaches that the Messiah will be a human king • Maimonides’ test for identifying the true Messiah • Why Judaism does not accept the Christian doctrine of a second coming • How Christianity transformed the Messiah from a human leader into a divine redeemer • The Jewish response to original sin and salvation through belief • Why Judaism teaches personal responsibility, repentance and direct return to God • The Jewish interpretation of Isaiah 53 • Whether Jeremiah’s “new covenant” replaces the Torah • Why God’s covenant with Israel remains eternal • The influence of Paul on the development of Christianity • Why Jews for Jesus and Messianic Judaism are considered forms of Christianity • How Jewish survival became one of Judaism’s strongest historical answers • Maimonides’ remarkable teaching about the possible role of Christianity and Islam in preparing humanity for the final redemption
This is not an attack on Christians. Millions of Christians sincerely love God, the Bible and the people of Israel. This presentation explains why Judaism cannot accept the Christian claims about Jesus while still respecting Christians as human beings created in the image of God.
The main biblical passages discussed include Isaiah 2, Isaiah 11, Isaiah 52–53, Jeremiah 31, Ezekiel 18, Ezekiel 36–37, Zephaniah 3, Zechariah 14, Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 30. The criteria established by Maimonides can be found in Mishneh Torah, Hilchot Melachim, chapters 11 and 12.
If you disagree, share the verses you believe answer these questions:
Where does the Hebrew Bible say that the Messiah will divide his mission between a first and second coming?
Where does it say that God will become a human being?
Where does it say that the eternal Torah will be canceled or replaced?
Let’s discuss the texts honestly and respectfully.
